keyChanges.title: Grimes County School Boards Approve $119B Terafab JETI Tax Deals 5-2 Amid Local Opposition
keyChanges.description: On July 14, 2026, Iola ISD and Anderson-Shiro CISD each voted 5-2 to approve all eight JETI school-property-tax agreements for TeraFab AI, LLC (SpaceX special-purpose entity) covering the proposed Terafab semiconductor complex near Gibbons Creek in Grimes County. Agreements grant a 10-year school M&O tax reduction per phase (freeze at ~50% of appraised value) in exchange for claims of up to $119B total investment across four phases, 4,234+ direct jobs, and ~22,000 acres. Phase 1 alone was previously filed at ~$10.37B; media also cite a ~$55B first-phase scale. SpaceX told districts that without the deals the project would likely relocate out of Texas (Arizona cited). Community opposition was strong over water use, noise/lighting, and loss of small-town character (Iola population ~300). School boards framed approvals as keeping the process alive, not final endorsement. Construction still needs Governor Abbott approval, three-party signing, and Comptroller filing—no permits or groundwater apps were on file as of mid-June reporting. SpaceX wants Phase 1 construction before year-end 2026.

positive_signals: Both Iola ISD and Anderson-Shiro CISD approved all eight JETI agreements (required school-district step)
Applications claim up to $119B investment and 4,234+ jobs across four phases
SpaceX stated intent to begin Phase 1 construction before end of 2026 if deals close
District leaders argue residual tax revenue still funds teachers and programs even with abatements
negative_signals: Votes were only 5-2—not consensus; public comment was largely opposed (water, identity, trust)
Deal is not final: still requires Governor Abbott approval and three-party execution before construction
SpaceX openly threatened to leave Texas without tax breaks—leverage, not manufacturing progress
As of June document reporting: no building permits, no groundwater applications filed despite 2026 construction claims
Project entity is TeraFab AI, LLC under SpaceX filings—not a proven Tesla-operated fab with semiconductor experience
Tax abatements transfer cost to state/local taxpayers; they do not solve talent, yield, or process-node execution risk
Geographic focus is Grimes County (Gibbons Creek), not demonstrated North Campus Austin fab groundbreaking

keyChanges.title: Gov. Abbott Terafab JETI Decision Deadline Passes With No Public Yes/No; Deal Still Not Locked
keyChanges.description: Under Texas JETI rules, Governor Greg Abbott shared the same 30-day window as the school districts after Comptroller acceptance on June 15, 2026—closing July 15. After the July 14 school-board approvals, KBTX reported on July 16 that Abbott’s decision remained unknown past the deadline. Law allows up to seven additional days to formally notify parties, so an answer could slip into the following week. If Abbott votes no, the school approvals are void and the deal dies; SpaceX filings state the project could leave Texas without the agreements. If yes, parties must still formally sign and file with the Comptroller before Phase 1 construction can start. Separately on July 16, Grimes County commissioners tabled a local ‘accountability’ resolution meant to set clearer industrial-project standards (water, lighting, noise, transparency)—signaling unresolved community and governance friction even as tax deals advance.

positive_signals: School-district approvals cleared one of two required political gates
Governor has a short additional notification window rather than an automatic rejection
County pause on accountability resolution was framed as allowing more public input, not killing the project
negative_signals: Abbott decision unknown after statutory July 15 deadline—project remains in limbo
A single gubernatorial no kills all eight school agreements regardless of 5-2 board votes
SpaceX has conditioned Texas siting on tax breaks; failure risk is explicit in filings
No public confirmation of Abbott yes by July 17 coverage—timeline for year-end construction already under pressure
Grimes County tabled manufacturer accountability resolution amid damaged public trust and water/noise concerns
Political process progress is not equivalent to fab equipment, process qualification, or first wafer

keyChanges.title: Samsung Process Tape-Out of Tesla AI5 on 2nm at Taylor Fab; Volume Still Mid/H2 2027
keyChanges.description: On/around July 13, 2026, multiple semiconductor and EV outlets reported that a Samsung Foundry principal engineer (James Kim) posted on LinkedIn that the Tesla–Samsung AI5 design reached process tape-out and is scheduled for manufacture at Samsung’s Taylor, Texas fab on Samsung’s latest 2nm node—then deleted the post after Korean media pickup. TrendForce, citing Yonhap, said this was the first concrete Samsung Foundry production-timeline disclosure for AI5; AI5 will be dual-sourced with TSMC, while Samsung is reported to take full AI6 and TSMC AI6.5. Samsung has been installing front-end/back-end tools at Taylor since late April and reaffirmed ramp production in 2027. Electrek and others note AI5 on 2nm (previously assumed more for AI6) implies improved 2nm yields, but volume vehicle-board supply is still guided mid-2027 / H2 2027—not 2026. Critical context: April 2026 already saw Musk claim AI5 design tape-out to both foundries; this week is Samsung process-specific readiness, not mass production. Cybercab and current vehicles still depend on older AI4/AI4.5 hardware while AI5 remains multi-year late vs original promises.

positive_signals: Samsung Foundry engineer disclosed AI5 process tape-out targeted for Taylor 2nm production
Dual-sourcing AI5 at Samsung and TSMC reduces single-foundry failure risk
Taylor fab equipment install and engineer deployment reported underway since late April 2026
AI5 on 2nm (vs prior assumption of only AI6 on 2nm) suggests Samsung yield story may be improving
negative_signals: Tape-out is not volume production—qualification wafers and customer sign-off still required
Samsung volume production of Tesla AI chips at Taylor still guided to H2 2027 / mid-2027, matching prior delay narrative
Disclosure came via a LinkedIn post that was deleted—not a formal Samsung customer press release
AI5 remains roughly two years late vs Musk’s earlier vehicle-integration promises; Cybercab launching on AI4
Prior reporting already tied AI6 slip (~6 months) to Samsung 2nm yield issues—2nm risk not retired
Musk has said Tesla needs several hundred thousand completed AI5 boards line-side before vehicle switchover—still distant
This is foundry outsourcing progress, not Terafab vertical-integration proof of Tesla/SpaceX making advanced logic themselves

categoryUpdate.latestStatus: Political/tax track advanced but not closed: Grimes County school boards approved eight SpaceX Terafab JETI deals (5-2 each) on July 14; Governor Abbott’s required decision was still unannounced after the July 15 deadline as of July 16 reporting. Separately, Samsung disclosed (via deleted LinkedIn post) AI5 process tape-out for 2nm at Taylor, with volume still mid/H2 2027—not a Terafab self-fab milestone.
categoryUpdate.nextMilestone: Public confirmation of Governor Abbott’s JETI yes/no and formal three-party signing; any Phase 1 construction permits/groundbreaking in Grimes County before year-end 2026; Samsung Taylor engineering samples / qualification progress toward 2027 volume AI5.
concerns: Abbott veto risk or delayed notification keeps $119B project in limbo despite school votes
No verified construction permits/groundwater filings as of last detailed document dump—2026 Phase 1 start is at risk
Community opposition and paused county accountability measures signal local friction
AI5 volume still mid-2027; tape-out headlines overstate near-term silicon supply
Terafab remains execution-heavy: tax incentives and foundry outsourcing do not prove Tesla/SpaceX can run advanced semiconductor manufacturing
Tier 1 Tesla outlets (Teslarati, TeslaNorth) had no substantive new Terafab coverage this week—story driven by local TX and Korean semi press

metadata.notes: Deduped vs hot context: skipped July 7 'cool news'/Cybercab rides mismatch, prior AI5 mid-2027 delay analysis as standalone item, and generic execution-risk essay. Included NEW school JETI votes, Abbott silence, and Samsung process tape-out (distinct from April design tape-out already noted). Tier 1 Tesla media had no new Terafab articles in range; primary sourcing from KBTX local reporting and TrendForce/Yonhap semiconductor coverage with Electrek corroboration only.
